item.title: 5G Bahrain eSIM Data | Batelco, Zain & STC Bahrain
item.description: The island is about 50 km across, so Bahrain eSIM coverage is not the puzzle it is in bigger countries — all three networks reach nearly everyone. The real decisions are different: do you want a prepaid bundle with a local number, or a travel eSIM you install before you fly? And, new for 2026, Bahrain’s regulator lets licensed operators issue international-only eSIMs that skip local registration entirely — a genuine change worth knowing before you land. This guide answers which carrier your Bahrain eSIM should ride, how each one sells to visitors, and where the few dead spots actually are.

item.title: 5G Belgium eSIM | Proximus, Orange & Base Coverage
item.description: The short answer: Belgium is one of the easiest connectivity markets in Europe, and that is exactly why picking a Belgium eSIM carrier is less dramatic than the comparisons suggest. On Ookla’s H1 2025 Speedtest data, Proximus is the fastest mobile network (median download 93.33 Mbps), Orange runs the fastest 5G (median 156.37 Mbps), and Telenet/BASE puts the most users on 5G (19.6% availability) — but the top three networks finish within about 13 Mbps of each other overall, and Ookla found no statistical difference between them for overall network quality. Downtown Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent or Bruges, any of the three will feel identical. Where the real decisions live: the Ardennes (the one region where coverage genuinely falls off), the EU quarter at 9am, the trains between cities, and the fact that Belgian prepaid SIMs require in-person ID registration, which most visitors are better off skipping entirely with a Belgium travel eSIM.

item.title: Australia eSIM Plans | Telstra, Optus & Vodafone
item.description: Choosing an Australia eSIM is really choosing between three national networks whose gap widens with every kilometre you put between yourself and the coast, because the continent is mostly empty — this guide maps which one fits your route. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Australia report, Optus was named the Best Mobile Network overall and the Best 5G Network in the country. The published carrier-level chart data in that same report covers Vodafone in full, with a Consistency Score of 86.4 and 5G availability of 82.5. Telstra does not win a head-to-head speed award in this dataset, but it owns the largest geographic footprint, which is the single most important fact for anyone leaving the coast. Which is why the right pick shifts with your route: a harbour-city stay and a long regional drive rarely want the same network.

item.title: Bangladesh eSIM | Grameenphone, Robi & Banglalink
item.description: A Bangladesh eSIM puts you on the same towers locals use, and here the towers matter more than the brand. Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index for August 2026 puts the median mobile download at 56.45 Mbps — 91st in the world, at 28 ms latency — and Cable.co.uk prices 1 GB of local data at about USD 0.23. So the real question is not whether to buy a Bangladesh eSIM, but which network it should hold. The failure cases Roami’s support team handles for Bangladesh are exactly what the coverage and registration sections below address plainly.

item.title: Prepaid Albania eSIM | Vodafone, One & ALBtelecom
item.description: Sorting out an Albania eSIM before you fly matters more here than in most of Europe, because EU roaming ends the moment your phone crosses the border. Albania has the most misleading price tag in European travel. The beaches, the guesthouses and the grilled trout in Theth all cost a fraction of what you would pay across the Adriatic — your phone bill is the one exception. First-time Albania eSIM setups come with predictable stumbling blocks — each section below takes on one of them.

item.title: Prepaid Azerbaijan eSIM | Azercell, Bakcell & Nar
item.description: Most “which Azerbaijan eSIM works here” pages assume the only question is price. It isn’t. In Azerbaijan the first surprise is registration: bring a phone from abroad, put a local SIM in it, and the device itself must be registered in the national IMEI database within 30 days or it gets blocked on every Azerbaijani network. A travel eSIM that issues no local number sidesteps that entirely. So the real question this guide answers is which carrier should your Azerbaijan eSIM ride on — and do you even want a local SIM at all? The three networks are not equal: Azercell reaches the Caucasus foothills, Bakcell is the cheap urban pick, and Nar is the budget alternative.

item.title: Prepaid Belarus eSIM | A1, MTS & Coverage
item.description: A Belarus eSIM rewards a different first question than the speed leagues ask. Most eSIM guides rank countries by speed; Belarus is better understood through price and paperwork. Local data is exceptionally cheap — Cable.co.uk’s 237-market index puts 1 GB at about USD 0.67, 66th worldwide — yet the median mobile download was just 18.55 Mbps at end-2025, per DataReportal. We keep this Belarus page updated as carrier policies shift, because the worst travel tech advice is a guide nobody has touched in two years.

item.title: Travel Argentina eSIM | Claro, Movistar & Personal
item.description:
If you are heading to Buenos Aires or Patagonia, this guide helps you pick an Argentina eSIM in a market where locals call a SIM card a “chip” and where the national ID, the DNI, sat at the center of every mobile registration for years. None of the steps below should take more than a few minutes — we clocked first-timers doing each.

Quick answer: For a short trip, a local network’s tourist plan is the least-effort option; for longer stays, buying local tends to win on cost per gigabyte. The sections below break down where Personal, Claro and Movistar each shine — and first-time eSIM users should begin at the activation walkthrough.

item.title: Unlimited Algeria eSIM | Djezzy, Mobilis & Ooredoo
item.description: An Algeria eSIM is the rare travel connectivity purchase that starts with paperwork, not price comparison — here is what visitors need to know first. Algeria is one of the few North African markets where you cannot simply walk into a shop and walk out with working mobile data. Every SIM card sold in the country must be registered against a passport and a local address. Every few months this guide is rebuilt around Roami’s Algeria activation logs and support tickets — press releases alone do not drive it.

item.title: Unlimited Bolivia eSIM Data | Entel, Tigo & Viva
item.description: Bolivia is the one country in South America where the carrier question is not about speed at all — it is about where the signal reaches. The national median mobile download sits at just 20.65 Mbps (Ookla, August 2026, 99th in the world), there is no commercial 5G yet, and the landscape does the rest: the altiplano sits at 3,600–4,000 m, the salt flats have no towers at all, and the Amazon basin eats every radio wave. Which Bolivia eSIM serves you well is therefore a coverage decision first and a price decision second.

item.title: 5G Colombia eSIM | Claro, Movistar & Tigo Coverage
item.description: Colombia’s mobile market just went through its biggest shake-up in a decade: 5G spectrum was auctioned in December 2023, commercial networks lit up in February 2024, and by the end of 2024 Claro had built 92% of the country’s 1,433 active 5G sites. That single fact reshapes the carrier question for any Colombia eSIM. Tigo and Movistar now share a combined network in many places, WOM is still mostly a 4G story, and the gap between “the fastest city network” and “the network that follows you up the mountain” is as wide as the Andes themselves. First-time Colombia eSIM setups come with predictable stumbling blocks — each section below takes on one of them.

item.title: 5G Croatia eSIM | Hrvatski Telekom, A1 & Telemach
item.description: The right Croatia eSIM is decided on the water, not in Zagreb: this guide ranks the networks the way you will actually use them — ferries, coves and cruise stops. Most country guides rank networks by capital-city speed. Croatia breaks that method, because the product most visitors buy is the coast: a ferry from Split to Hvar, a week in a Korčula cove, or an eight-hour cruise stop in Dubrovnik. None of the Croatia steps below should take more than a few minutes — we clocked first-timers doing each.

item.title: Czech Republic eSIM Data | O2, T-Mobile & Vodafone
item.description: Prague spoils you. In the capital, all three Czech networks deliver fast, dependable data, and a Czech Republic eSIM works the moment you land. The country’s median mobile download sits at 92.26 Mbps — 49th in Ookla’s August 2026 global index — with a median 5G connection reaching 160.54 Mbps, and 1 GB of data costs about USD 3.12 per Cable.co.uk’s 237-market table. That price looks average globally but is the highest in its own region, so the purchase decision is less about cost than geography: the moment your itinerary adds Brno, Ostrava, Český Krumlov or a rail branch line, which network your Czech Republic eSIM rides on starts to matter. We answer the same handful of Czech Republic questions every week in support, so this page collects the real ones, worded the way travelers actually ask them.

item.title: Prepaid Bulgaria eSIM | A1, Vivacom & Yettel Coverage
item.description: Few destinations split the “best network” question by geography as sharply as Bulgaria. The national numbers are startling on paper: a median mobile download of 203.13 Mbps, 10th fastest in the world on Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index for August 2026, and a median 5G download of 282.70 Mbps, ranked 11th globally. Local prepaid data has been sold in euros since 1 January 2026, in quantities most western European carriers would call lavish: 15 GB for under €8, and 100 GB for around €41. So which Bulgaria eSIM carrier should you buy? The answer depends almost entirely on your map. Sofia and Plovdiv, the Black Sea coast at Varna and Burgas, and the ski slopes above Bansko behave like three different countries. This guide compares the three carriers, the published visitor prices, mountain and coastal coverage, cross-border rules and every activation step. Between our own test lines and the questions travelers send us, the Bulgaria quirks worth knowing are all covered below — including the ones carriers would rather skip.

item.title: Prepaid Chile eSIM Plans | Entel, Movistar & Claro
item.description: Picking a Chile eSIM means planning for 4,300 km of contrast, from Santiago’s fast networks to the dead zones of the Carretera Austral — this guide walks the whole length of it. Chile’s mobile map is stretched the same way. A profile that is brilliant in Santiago can hand you nothing at all on the Carretera Austral, and the carrier that holds one bar in Torres del Paine is rarely the one that wins a downtown speed test. Two buying rules changed recently and both catch visitors out: a Chilean prepaid chip is no longer plug-and-play, and the phone you brought with you starts a countdown the moment a local SIM goes in. Where Chile’s carriers disagree with the marketing copy, we say so — check the registration section for the fine print that actually bites.

item.title: Prepaid Costa Rica eSIM | Kölbi, Claro & Movistar
item.description: Bottom line: On paper, Claro wins Costa Rica eSIM carriers outright — a median download of 84.51 Mbps against Kölbi’s 36.79 and Liberty’s 39.46, plus the best gaming score and the fastest network in 8 of the 10 largest cities (Ookla, H1 2025). In the rainforest, the ranking flips. Kölbi, the state-owned ICE network, runs more towers than anyone else and is the carrier that still has signal on the park roads — which matters if your itinerary includes Manuel Antonio, Monteverde or the Osa Peninsula. Tourists can buy a Kölbi prepaid SIM on arrival with just a passport, but its eSIM route runs through a store visit. If you want data working before you land, a Costa Rica travel eSIM skips the counter entirely — and free eSIM trial lets you test the network at no cost. This guide gets rebuilt every few months from what Roami’s own activation logs and support tickets show about Costa Rica, not just from press releases.

item.title: Travel Cambodia eSIM | Smart, Cellcard & Metfone
item.description: A Cambodia eSIM sits in a market that is both among the cheapest on earth for data and brand new to 5G — this guide splits those two questions apart. Cambodia is an unusual eSIM market in two directions at once. Local data costs pennies — Cable.co.uk ranks it 5th of 237 countries at roughly USD 0.12 per gigabyte — and yet commercial 5G only went live on 1 January 2026, when the telecoms ministry cleared Smart, Cellcard and Metfone to light up the first phase of their new networks. So the question “is 5G fast enough in Cambodia?” has a short answer (it is early days) and a useful one: what actually matters for a Cambodia eSIM right now is 4G consistency outside Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, plus knowing how SIM registration works at the airport.

item.title: Travel Cyprus eSIM | Cyta, Epic & PrimeTel Coverage
item.description: Cyprus is the one European destination where the carrier question is not only “which network is fastest” but “which side of the island are you on?” The Republic of Cyprus in the south is served by Cyta, Epic (formerly MTN Cyprus), PrimeTel and Cablenet. The Turkish-administered north runs on completely separate Turkish operators — Turkcell KKTC and Telsim Vodafone — that a standard Cyprus eSIM does not include. Cross the Green Line and your southern eSIM simply stops, and your phone may quietly grab a northern signal. This guide answers which southern carrier your eSIM should ride, how to buy as a visitor, and how to handle the line.

item.title: Unlimited Canada eSIM Data | Rogers, Bell & Telus
item.description: Which carrier should your Canada eSIM connect to? The three national networks are not interchangeable. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Canada report, Bell was the Best and Fastest 5G provider with a median 5G download of 171.17 Mbps. Rogers delivered the best video experience (86.03) and the highest 5G availability (86.7%). TELUS was the most consistent network overall (85.6%). Which one is “best” depends entirely on where you are going — the best eSIM carrier for Canada is a routing decision, not a brand decision. This Canada guide is written by people who sell and support eSIMs daily, so it favors practical trade-offs over brochure claims.

item.title: Unlimited China eSIM | China Mobile, Unicom & Telecom
item.description:
A China eSIM looks, on the surface, like any other travel purchase: pick a data allowance, scan a QR code, land, connect. That part is genuinely easy. Treat this as the pre-flight China briefing — the one we would send a friend, jargon removed.

Quick answer: Most travellers in China will be happiest with plug-and-play; Great Wall makes sense for tighter budgets and city-only trips. Run your device through the compatibility checker first — the step China visitors skip and later regret.

item.title: 5G Dominican Republic eSIM | Claro, Altice & Viva
item.description: The Dominican Republic eSIM question is really a resort question. If you are spending a week at an all-inclusive in Punta Cana, the hotel network will cover the lobby, buffet and pool deck — and quietly fall apart in your room, at the quiet pool, or the moment you leave the gates for an excursion. A Dominican Republic eSIM keeps you on real carrier networks instead, and since your phone must be eSIM-capable and unlocked to use one, run it through the compatibility checker before you buy anything.

item.title: Europe eSIM | Vodafone, Orange & Telekom Coverage
item.description: A Europe eSIM is decided before you land, because five countries in two weeks is a normal European trip, not an extreme one — and that single fact changes the arithmetic that works elsewhere. This guide helps you pick a region-wide strategy instead of buying five local ones. A local SIM is the cheapest option in almost every other region on earth; in Europe, the question is which country’s local SIM, purchased how many times, and what happens when the train crosses into the next market.

item.title: Finland eSIM Plans | Elisa, Telia & DNA Coverage
item.description: A Finland eSIM drops you into one of the world’s best mobile markets, and this guide covers the part that actually trips visitors up: getting onto the network. If a country were ever built for eSIMs, it is Finland. In Opensignal’s Global Network Excellence Index for Q1 2025, Finland ranked second in the world for overall mobile network experience — ahead of every country except South Korea. In the Ookla Speedtest Connectivity Report for Finland, 1H 2025, DNA took the Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network titles with a median 5G download of 242.64 Mbps, while Elisa and Telia were close behind on 5G speed. And 1 GB of local data costs about USD 0.52, less than a fifth of the global average. Your Finland eSIM inherits all of this — the real question is not whether you will have fast data, but which of the three carriers your eSIM should attach to in the places you are actually going. Treat this as the pre-flight Finland briefing — the one we would send a friend, jargon removed.

item.title: Prepaid Denmark eSIM | TDC, Telia & Telenor Coverage
item.description: A Denmark eSIM comes with a twist few guides mention: Denmark is two destinations at once. It is an EU member, so a Danish-issued SIM carries “roam like at home” rights across most of Europe — and it is one of the world’s most digital societies, where 99 percent of the population is online and many shops have quietly stopped accepting banknotes. Both facts shape how you should get online there, and neither favors the approach most travelers default to. This guide walks through the roaming rules first, then the networks, how a travel eSIM compares, the arrival logistics at Copenhagen Airport, and the places where coverage genuinely thins out. Each claim here points to a named source — the list at the end is worth a look before paying for Denmark.

item.title: Prepaid Estonia eSIM | Telia, Elisa & Tele2 Coverage
item.description: An Estonia eSIM sounds simple in e-Estonia, but since January 2024 every local prepaid needs in-person ID registration — this guide explains what that means for visitors. Estonia is a 45-by-150 km country that pitches itself as “e-Estonia,” so the question here is not whether the networks are good — on Ookla’s H2 2025 awards, Elisa won both Best and Fastest 5G with a median 5G download of 336.49 Mbps — but whether a foreign visitor can actually get onto one. Since 1 January 2024, every new prepaid SIM (and eSIM) sold in Estonia must be registered against a passport or EU ID card in person, which quietly removes the “walk up and buy a local eSIM” option that exists in most countries. This guide answers three things: which of the three networks your eSIM should ride, how the prepaid-ID wall changes your buying path, and what EU roaming really means when you hop the Tallinn–Helsinki ferry. Our test lines plus the questions travelers actually send us shape what’s below — Estonia quirks included, even the ones carriers would rather skip.

item.title: Prepaid Fiji eSIM | Vodafone, Digicel & Telecom Fiji
item.description: Choosing a Fiji eSIM should follow your island sequence — Nadi, the Mamanucas, the Yasawa ferry chain — not a speed-test league table, and this guide is built exactly that way. Most Fiji trips are really a sequence: land at Nadi, cross to the Mamanucas, ride the Yasawa ferry chain north, maybe loop back through Pacific Harbour and Suva before a side flight to Taveuni. That sequence should decide how you buy connectivity — because signal strength on Viti Levu tells you almost nothing about Day 5 on a Yasawa resort island. This guide walks the country the way you will actually travel it, then covers the two-operator market and the practicalities (paid resort Wi-Fi, Fijian dollars, cyclone season) that most guides skip. Where Fiji’s carriers disagree with the marketing copy, we say so — check the registration section for the fine print that actually bites.

item.title: Travel Ecuador eSIM | Claro, Movistar & CNT Coverage
item.description: In brief: On the mainland, a Claro eSIM is the coverage pick — Ookla named Claro Ecuador the fastest mobile network in 1H 2026 at a median 54.98 Mbps, with reach into parts of the Amazon that no rival matches. Movistar Ecuador, now owned by Millicom and gradually rebranding as Tigo, is nearly as fast and the most consistent network in the country at 91.8%. CNT EP, the state operator, is the budget choice with respectable urban coverage. In the Galápagos, every Ecuador eSIM behaves the same: usable in the three port towns, silent everywhere else. A travel eSIM roaming Claro or Movistar wins for most one-to-three-week trips — no passport registration, no store queue. Roami’s free trial eSIM lets you test the waters, and the code WEB20 cuts 20% from Ecuador eSIM plans. If you have installed a travel eSIM before, you can skim straight to the Ecuador carrier comparison; the activation section is written for absolute first-timers.

item.title: Travel Ethiopia eSIM | Ethio Telecom & Safaricom
item.description: Ethiopia has exactly two mobile carriers, and choosing between them is easier than in most countries: Ethio Telecom owns the network almost everywhere, and Safaricom Ethiopia is the challenger that matters mainly in Addis Ababa and a growing list of cities. But the honest answer to “which Ethiopia eSIM carrier is best” starts somewhere else entirely — with the fact that Ethiopia is one of the few tourist destinations where the government can and does switch the internet off by region. This guide covers the carrier choice, the registration paperwork, where the coverage actually ends, and how to plan around an internet shutdown, because no other article on Ethiopia eSIMs puts those four things in one place.

item.title: Unlimited Egypt eSIM | Vodafone, Orange & Etisalat
item.description: Egypt is one of the cheapest countries in the world for mobile data — and one of the most bureaucratic to buy it in. An Egypt eSIM is how you get the first without the second: local networks priced at roughly USD 0.65 per GB, no branch visit, no passport photocopy, no signing a paper contract at a counter in Cairo. Before buying anything, confirm your phone is eligible with the device compatibility checker — everything else in this guide assumes a working, unlocked device.

item.title: 5G Germany eSIM | Telekom, Vodafone & O2 Coverage
item.description: Choosing a Germany eSIM means choosing between three national networks, and none of them is the automatic answer. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Germany report, Telekom was named Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network, with the highest Speedtest Connectivity Score at 78.87. Vodafone posted the strongest rural reach among the big three, and O2 led on 5G availability at 72.4 percent. Which one serves you best comes down to the ground you cover — the right German carrier is a routing decision, not a logo decision. Every few months this guide is rebuilt around Roami’s Germany activation logs and support tickets — press releases alone do not drive it.

item.title: 5G Hong Kong eSIM | CMHK, csl & SmarTone Coverage
item.description: A Hong Kong eSIM is the quickest way online in one of Asia’s most connected markets — and one of the cheapest. Local data costs about USD 0.82 per gigabyte, 82nd of the 237 markets Cable.co.uk tracks and far under the global average, while DataReportal counts 7.10 million internet users in Hong Kong, China (96.0% penetration) on 17.4 million mobile connections. The infrastructure a visitor profile rides on is dense, mature and fast. Each claim here points to a named source — the list at the end is worth a look before paying for Hong Kong.

item.title: 5G Indonesia eSIM | Telkomsel, Indosat & XL Axiata
item.description: Indonesia is an archipelago of about 17,000 islands, and its mobile map behaves like one. Bali and Jakarta get speeds that feel European; a ferry crossing to the Gilis drops you to a single bar, and a Raja Ampat homestay runs on whatever the nearest tower reaches at low tide. Choosing an Indonesia eSIM is therefore two decisions rather than one: which network you attach to, and whether your handset is even allowed onto it.

item.title: Hungary eSIM | Magyar Telekom, Vodafone & Yettel
item.description: A Hungary eSIM comes with unusually good speed numbers for the price, and this guide walks the three national networks so you know which one fits your route. Hungary is the rare European destination where the speed numbers are almost embarrassing — in a good way. In Ookla’s H1 2025 connectivity report, Yettel recorded a median 5G download of 369.08 Mbps, among the fastest readings in the region, while Magyar Telekom countered with the country’s highest 5G availability and the best video score. Three carriers, three genuinely different strengths, and a traveller-facing question that mostly comes down to where between Budapest and Lake Balaton your days are spent. Coverage and registration below are written from Roami’s own Hungary support tickets — including the cases that went wrong.

item.title: Prepaid Ghana eSIM Data | MTN, Telecel & AirtelTigo
item.description: Ghana is one of the easiest places in Africa to afford mobile data and one of the more procedurally strict places to buy it. The August 2026 Speedtest Global Index puts its median mobile download at 50.87 Mbps, 95th in the world. Cable.co.uk averages 1 GB of local data at about USD 0.40 — 33rd cheapest of 237 markets, against a global average of USD 2.59. DataReportal counted 38.3 million mobile connections at the start of 2025. What none of that tells you is how a Ghana eSIM gets into your phone, because this market adds two twists: a cash-and-Mobile-Money economy, and a biometric SIM registration law enforced by the National Communications Authority (NCA). Every Ghana step below runs short; we have watched first-timers finish each one inside a few minutes. The price tables below also show what an eSIM in Ghana costs against buying at an airport counter.

item.title: Prepaid Guatemala eSIM Data | Claro, Tigo & Movistar
item.description: The verdict up front: Guatemala eSIM carriers come down to a straight duel — Claro and Tigo control the entire market, with no third national network since Movistar folded into Claro in 2019. The official regulator’s numbers give Tigo roughly 56% of mobile lines to Claro’s 44%, but Ookla’s 2H 2025 report gives Claro nearly every performance trophy: a median download of 81.14 Mbps against Tigo’s 28.34, a 5G median of 409.62 Mbps, and the best consistency, video and gaming scores (Ookla). Tourists can buy prepaid service from either — and both sell eSIMs, Claro even self-serve by QR code — with a valid passport as the only document the law demands. Data is also among the cheapest you’ll touch on this continent: about USD 1.17 per GB. If you’d rather be online before immigration than queueing at a counter, start with a Guatemala travel eSIM or test the network with a free test eSIM. Support gets the same handful of Guatemala questions every week; this page collects the real ones, worded the way travelers actually ask.

item.title: Travel France eSIM | Orange, SFR & Bouygues Coverage
item.description: Picking a France eSIM means choosing between four networks that split the wins — speed, price and shop-only tourist rules — and this guide breaks down each one. If you read nothing else: France runs four mobile networks, and only one of them sells a tourist eSIM you can buy without setting foot in a shop. On speed, Orange is the network to beat: a median 5G download of 281.3 Mbps, the fastest overall network at 122.77 Mbps, and the best 5G consistency (77.9%) in the country per Ookla’s H2 2024 report.

item.title: Travel Greece eSIM | Cosmote, Vodafone & Nova Coverage
item.description: The best Greece eSIM depends on your island group, not the brand logo — this guide matches the three national networks to the routes you will actually sail. Greece runs on three national networks, and they are not the same. On Ookla’s Speedtest Connectivity Report for the first half of 2025, Cosmote took both the Best Mobile Network award and the Best 5G Network award, with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 77.64. Vodafone followed at 73.42, and Nova (the network formerly called Wind) closed the field at 70.59. The right network is the one that still works on the ferry route you booked.

item.title: Travel Iceland eSIM | Síminn, Vodafone & Nova Coverage
item.description: Iceland breaks every rule of the usual “which carrier is best” article, in three ways. The airport is actually a good place to buy a physical SIM — but it sells no eSIMs at all. There is no SIM registration paperwork — Iceland is one of Europe’s anonymous-prepaid holdouts. And the network question is not Reykjavík vs the countryside: it is how far off Route 1 you plan to drive, because beyond roughly 90% 4G coverage along the Ring Road, the F-roads and the interior highlands are silent on every network. This guide works through all three, plus the EEA-roaming detail that changes the math for European visitors. We keep this Iceland page updated as carrier policies shift, because the worst travel tech advice is a guide nobody has touched in two years.

item.title: Unlimited India eSIM | Jio, Airtel & Vi Coverage
item.description: Choosing an India eSIM means matching the network to your itinerary: three private operators and one state-run giant split the map, and this guide shows who wins where. On Ookla’s 2H 2024 India report, Jio was the fastest mobile provider with a median 5G download of 258.54 Mbps, Airtel led video and 5G gaming experience, and Vi trailed on raw speed. Match the network to the states you are actually travelling through, not to the adverts. Installed a travel eSIM before? Skim straight to the India carrier comparison — the activation section is written for absolute first-timers.

item.title: 5G Ireland eSIM | Vodafone, Three & Eir Coverage
item.description: Picking an Ireland eSIM comes down to the roads you will actually drive — this guide maps which of the three networks wins where. Ireland’s three networks trade wins by metric and by county. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Ireland report, Three was the Best Mobile Network with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 74.84, Vodafone posted the highest Consistency Score at 83.5, and Eir led 5G Availability at 82.6 percent. Choose for the roads you will actually drive, not for the headline award.

item.title: Jordan eSIM Plans | Zain, Orange & Umniah Coverage
item.description: A Jordan eSIM choice splits with the country itself: fast 5G in Amman’s tech hub versus a lifeline signal on the southern tourist route — this guide covers both ends. Jordan is a small kingdom with a split personality, and its connectivity splits with it. In Amman, a genuine tech hub of startups, coworking spaces and the Zain Innovation Campus, you want the fastest 5G you can hold. Four hundred kilometres south, in the camps of Wadi Rum and the canyons of Petra, you want whichever network keeps a bar of signal alive. Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index put Jordan’s median mobile download at 48.53 Mbps in August 2026 — 81st worldwide, well below the 109.05 Mbps global median — while Cable.co.uk prices a gigabyte of local data at about USD 0.76, cheaper than most of Europe. Which Jordan eSIM fits you depends on which of the two Jordans you are visiting.

item.title: Kenya eSIM | Safaricom, Airtel & Telkom Coverage
item.description: Kenya is the rare safari destination where carrier choice genuinely changes your trip: Safaricom’s network reaches into the national parks where your itinerary actually spends its days, while the cheaper alternatives thin out exactly where the wildlife starts. This guide answers the real questions — which Kenya eSIM carrier works inside the Maasai Mara, whether you can buy a Safaricom eSIM as a visitor, what the mandatory SIM registration involves, and why M-Pesa is the one thing a data-only eSIM cannot give you. If you have read other articles that stop at “Safaricom is best, buy an eSIM,” the registration rules, the park-by-park coverage reality and the airport-purchase logistics below are the missing half.

item.title: Prepaid Iran eSIM | MCI, Irancell & Rightel Coverage
item.description:
An Iran eSIM breaks the standard travel-connectivity playbook more completely than anywhere else — the exceptions start the moment you land, and almost nobody tells you before departure. Everything below comes from our own test lines and real traveler questions — the Iran quirks worth knowing, including the ones carriers would rather skip.

Quick answer: Sort it before you fly, install it before you land, and choose MCI or Irancell based on whether your route leaves the big cities — the full comparison below shows which is which. One question gets forgotten most by Iran visitors; the phone compatibility list answers it.

item.title: Prepaid Israel eSIM | Pelephone, Partner & Cellcom
item.description: An Israel eSIM rarely fails for distance, and this guide covers the real offline triggers, from Shabbat hours to slow passport registration. Israel is roughly the size of New Jersey, and 91.1% of its population is online. Cell coverage is effectively a solved problem: four national networks blanket the coastal plain, the Jerusalem hills, the Galilee and the road corridors through the Negev. Yet travelers still end up offline here, and almost never because of distance. They end up offline because the airport counter was closed for Shabbat, because their passport registration took longer than the connection they needed to make, or because they assumed a plan that works in Tel Aviv follows them across the Allenby Bridge. This guide is organized around that reality — the map first, then the operators, then the itinerary, then the small print that actually decides whether your Israel eSIM serves the whole trip. Where Israel’s carriers disagree with the marketing copy, we say so — the registration section holds the fine print that bites.

item.title: Prepaid Kazakhstan eSIM | Beeline, Kcell & Tele2
item.description: Choosing between Kazakhstan eSIM carriers is really two decisions in one. In the two cities that matter to most itineraries — Almaty and Astana — Kcell runs the fastest network in the country, with a median 5G download of 368.95 Mbps in Ookla’s H1 2025 report. But across the vast distances between cities, the picture flips: Tele2 took the Best Mobile Network award overall (Connectivity Score 72.37) and was the fastest provider in nine of Kazakhstan’s regions, while Beeline — which has skipped commercial 5G entirely — still holds the widest rural 4G footprint. And whichever carrier you land on, data is cheap: Cable.co.uk prices a gigabyte in Kazakhstan at about USD 0.41, roughly a sixth of the global average. Every Kazakhstan step below runs short; we have watched first-timers finish each one inside a few minutes.

item.title: Travel Iraq eSIM | Zain, Asiacell & Korek Coverage
item.description: Iraq sells some of the cheapest mobile data on earth and makes you work harder than most countries to use it. On Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index for August 2026, Iraq’s median mobile download sits at 72.23 Mbps — 62nd in the world, with 19 ms latency — while Cable.co.uk prices 1 GB of Iraqi mobile data at roughly USD 1.07, 97th of 237 markets against a USD 2.59 global average. DataReportal counted 48.1 million mobile connections at the start of 2025, 103 percent of the population, on top of 38.0 million internet users. The catch is structural: Iraq is really two mobile markets under two regulators, and the best Iraq eSIM for your trip depends on which side of the internal border you spend your days — federal Iraq or the Kurdistan Region. We have set up enough of these plans to know which steps people get wrong, and the activation guide below calls those out explicitly. No Iraq eSIM carrier sells to visitors entirely online, which is why the pre-departure route matters here more than anywhere.

item.title: Travel Italy eSIM | TIM, Vodafone & WindTre Coverage
item.description: The deciding question is simple — which carrier should your Italy eSIM connect to? The four national networks are not interchangeable. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Italy report, Vodafone was named the Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network, with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 75.95. WINDTRE posted the highest 5G availability at 74.8 percent. TIM led the video streaming experience at 76.53. Iliad offered the best headline value and the highest user rating at 3.34. Which one is best depends entirely on where you are going, so the best eSIM carrier for Italy is a routing decision, not a brand decision. This is the Italy version of the talk we give friends the night before they fly, stripped of jargon.

item.title: Travel Kuwait eSIM | Zain, Ooredoo & STC Coverage
item.description: Few destinations make an eSIM look this good on paper. Kuwait ranked 3rd in the world for mobile download speed in Ookla’s August 2026 Global Index, with a national median of 399.92 Mbps — the three carriers spent years outbuilding each other on 5G, and it shows. The interesting question for a Kuwait eSIM is therefore not “will it be fast?” (it will) but “which of Zain, Ooredoo and stc fits your stay, and what does getting connected cost you in paperwork?” We answer the same handful of Kuwait questions every week in support, so this page collects the real ones, worded the way travelers actually ask them.

item.title: Unlimited Japan eSIM Data | Docomo, au & SoftBank
item.description: Pick a network, not a brand: which carrier should your Japan eSIM connect to? Japan’s four national networks are not interchangeable. On Ookla’s 2H 2024 Japan report, Rakuten Mobile was the most consistent network at 89.9%, SoftBank offered the best video and gaming experiences, NTT Docomo led on 5G availability at 43%, and au balanced city and rural reach. Which one is best depends on where you are going, because the best eSIM carrier for Japan is a routing decision, not a brand decision. After guiding enough travelers through their first Japan eSIM, we know the usual confusion points; the sections below address them one by one.

item.title: 5G Luxembourg eSIM | POST, Tango & Orange Coverage
item.description: A Luxembourg eSIM may matter less than you think — the country is 82 km long, and most “which carrier” guides assume a place big enough that the answer varies by region. The honest opening line is: for many visitors, the carrier barely matters — and for EU arrivals it may not matter at all, because Roam Like at Home lets your home SIM work here at domestic rates. What follows explains when carrier choice is real (business travellers in Kirchberg, cross-border workers, non-EU visitors) and when it is not, plus the one rule that does affect everyone: Luxembourg’s prepaid-SIM registration law.

item.title: 5G Macau eSIM Plans | CTM, 3 & SmarTone Coverage
item.description: A Macau eSIM decision is unusually simple on paper — one dominant operator — and this guide covers the recent twist: the network that just disappeared and what remains. Macau is the rare destination where the carrier question answers itself. One operator, CTM, holds 53.3% of the mobile market and 96.8% of the broadband market, and it just absorbed the competition: after SmarTone quit mobile service in late 2024, CTM completed its acquisition of 3 Macau, whose mobile network will close on 30 November 2026. What remains is a two-network territory — CTM and China Telecom (Macau) — squeezed onto just 33 km² of land, where Ookla measured CTM’s median download at 176.04 Mbps, the fastest in the territory. In practice, a Macau eSIM is less about choosing a carrier and more about making sure your data survives the border crossings that bring most visitors here. Experienced with travel eSIMs? Head straight for the Macau carrier comparison; activation below assumes zero prior experience.

item.title: 5G Mauritius eSIM | Orange, Emtel & MTML Coverage
item.description: A Mauritius eSIM for visitors works differently from the local prepaid market, and this guide covers what tourists can actually buy. Mauritius runs one of the Indian Ocean’s most tourist-friendly connectivity markets — unlimited 5G tourist SIMs for a flat Rs 1,500 — and simultaneously one of its least understood: visitors can no longer buy the cheap local prepaid packages at all. Those are restricted to residents with local ID and proof of address, a rule verified across operator counters as recently as February 2026. This guide covers what that means for your wallet, the my.t vs Emtel vs Chili decision, the coverage reality inside Black River Gorges, and the Rodrigues question that almost every Mauritius article gets wrong.

item.title: Prepaid Lithuania eSIM | Telia, Bitė & Tele2 Coverage
item.description: A Lithuania eSIM is easy in the cities and subtle at the border, and this guide explains the Latvia-and-Poland crossing rule almost nobody covers. Lithuania quietly runs one of the better mobile markets in Eastern Europe: three competitive national operators, 5G across the major cities, and data priced well below the global average. It is also a country shaped by its borders — most visitors arrive for Vilnius but end up crossing into Latvia or Poland at some point, and what happens to your data connection at that border depends on a distinction almost nobody explains. This guide starts with the economics, then works through the operators, the practicalities of buying and paying, the airports, the coast, and the border-crossing logic. Coverage and registration below are written from Roami’s own Lithuania support tickets — including the cases that went wrong.

item.title: Prepaid Malaysia eSIM | Maxis, CelcomDigi & U Mobile
item.description: A Malaysia eSIM choice depends on which of the country’s two markets you are visiting, and on a shared wholesale 5G network that makes the differences between carriers subtler than they look — this guide untangles them. Malaysia is two markets wearing one flag. The Peninsula — KL, Penang, Johor — is a dense, fast, 5G-rich urban strip. East Malaysia, the Borneo states of Sabah and Sarawak, is a coverage frontier where the map thins between towns. The carrier you pick matters far more in the second than the first, and there is a structural quirk most guides miss: Malaysia’s 5G runs on a single wholesale network (DNB) that every operator resells, so 5G coverage is near-identical between carriers — the real difference is 4G reach and price. This guide walks the KLIA arrival, the MCMC passport rule, and which network to ride where.

item.title: Prepaid Mongolia eSIM | Mobicom, Unitel & Skytel
item.description: A Mongolia eSIM starts with distance, not brand: how far outside Ulaanbaatar you are going decides everything, and this guide works through the Unitel versus Mobicom call with the airport detail others miss. Mongolia is the country where “which carrier is best” is the wrong first question — the right one is “how far outside Ulaanbaatar am I going, and for how many days.” The capital has fast, cheap, genuinely modern mobile internet; the Gobi, the Altai and the Khövsgöl shorelines operate on a different physics entirely, where coverage means the nearest ger camp and not the trailhead. This guide covers the Unitel vs Mobicom decision with the airport-tourist-eSIM detail other articles miss, the registration rules, and a region-by-region plan for the world’s least densely populated country. This is the Mongolia version of the talk we give friends the night before they fly, stripped of jargon.

item.title: Travel Maldives eSIM | Dhiraagu & Ooredoo Coverage
item.description: There is no mainland grid to fall back on here — the Maldives is 1,192 coral islands strung across 26 atolls, joined only by speedboat and seaplane, with two licensed networks to carry your Maldives eSIM between them. So the decision is not “who is quickest downtown” but “who still has bars when a transfer sets you down at a resort 90 km from Malé.” Dhiraagu holds the wider spread of inhabited islands and resort atolls; Ooredoo is strongest exactly where most arrivals touch down first, in Malé and Hulhumalé. Choose wrong and your tourist eSIM becomes a dead rectangle the moment the capital slips out of sight behind you.

item.title: Travel Mexico eSIM | Telcel, AT&T & Movistar Coverage
item.description: Mexico’s three national networks pull apart sharply once you leave the cities. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Mexico report, Telcel was named both Best Mobile Network overall and Best 5G Network, with a consistency score of 90.5% and a Speed Score of 64.11. AT&T Mexico and Movistar sit behind on every measured metric, and a fourth name in the data, ALTAN Redes, is the wholesale network that smaller brands ride on rather than a line you buy yourself. What settles the choice of a Mexico eSIM is your route, not the brand. If Mexico’s carriers oversell in their marketing, we call it out — see the registration section for the fine print that matters.

item.title: Unlimited Latvia eSIM | LMT, Tele2 & Bite Coverage
item.description: Latvia is the cheapest Baltic capital to fly into and one of the EU’s most affordable mobile markets — but it has a detail most travel guides skip: every local SIM, physical or eSIM, must be registered against your passport at the point of sale. That single rule is why the eSIM-bought-before-you-fly route is worth more here than the price comparison alone suggests. This guide covers the LMT vs Tele2 vs Bite decision with real plan structures, the Riga airport buying logistics, and the one genuinely differentiating feature of this market — Baltic-wide roaming that turns a Latvia eSIM into a Lithuania-and-Estonia travel pass.

item.title: Unlimited Malta eSIM | Epic, GO & Melita Coverage
item.description: A Malta eSIM is hard to get wrong and easy to overthink — this guide covers the three small decisions that matter, from Comino’s Blue Lagoon to airport kiosk registration. The islands are 316 square kilometers, all three networks blanket the populated areas, and English is an official language — so the real decisions are smaller and more specific than most guides pretend: which carrier covers Comino’s Blue Lagoon on your day-trip morning, what the passport registration at the airport kiosk involves, and how the EU roam-like-at-home rules change the math for European visitors. This guide answers those, plus the detail most articles miss entirely: Malta has three carriers, and the third one is absent from almost every tourist article.

item.title: 5G Morocco eSIM | Maroc Telecom, Orange & inwi Coverage
item.description: Which carrier should your Morocco eSIM connect to? For most trips the answer is Maroc Telecom, and the data is unusually lopsided: in Ookla’s 2H 2024 Speedtest Connectivity Report, Maroc Telecom was the fastest provider in eight of Morocco’s nine largest cities, won the best mobile video experience (70.89), and posted a network consistency score of 89.2% — while also being the only one of the three carriers to publish tourist eSIM offers with real prices on its own website. inwi and Orange are credible alternatives in the cities, but neither matches the incumbent’s reach once the road climbs into the Atlas or turns off the main highway. The rebuild cycle runs on Roami’s own Morocco activation data and tickets, with press releases as a secondary input.

item.title: 5G Netherlands eSIM | KPN, VodafoneZiggo & Odido
item.description: The Netherlands is the most connected country most people visit without noticing. Cities are dense, networks are dense, and Ookla’s H1 2025 report shows a genuine three-way race: Odido posting the fastest medians in the country (216.3 Mbps all-technology, 272.74 Mbps on 5G), KPN Mobile winning on 5G consistency (88.6% of samples above 25 Mbps down), and Vodafone holding the broad consumer middle. A Netherlands eSIM rides all of that — the real decisions are which network your plan attaches to and what you expect from the places where Dutch flatness ends: the Wadden Islands, the forests of the Veluwe, the trains between them. Nothing anonymous made it into this guide; the closing source list covers every Netherlands figure.

item.title: 5G North Macedonia eSIM | Makedonski Telekom & A1
item.description: North Macedonia has some of the cheapest mobile data in Europe and one genuinely confusing quirk: whether Skopje Airport even has a carrier kiosk is a matter of dispute between sources. That uncertainty, plus mandatory passport registration and a Western Balkans roaming landscape where the three operators differ sharply, makes this a country where ten minutes of pre-trip reading saves a wasted airport hour. This North Macedonia eSIM guide covers the A1 vs Telekom vs MTEL decision with real plan structures, the Lake Ohrid and Matka Canyon coverage reality, and the roam-like-at-home pact among the six Western Balkans countries that most articles never mention.

item.title: Nicaragua eSIM | Claro, Movistar & Tigo Coverage
item.description:
How to choose a Nicaragua eSIM

A Nicaragua eSIM decision starts with an unusual fact: there is no long list of carriers to compare. Two networks — Claro and Tigo — divide essentially the whole market, neither sells an eSIM directly to visitors, and every line bought locally goes through a registration step. What matters instead is which network your profile roams on, whether your itinerary includes the Caribbean coast, and how you handle SIM registration. That is a different decision from most of Latin America, and this guide follows it. We keep this Nicaragua page updated as carrier policies shift, because the worst travel tech advice is a guide nobody has touched in two years.

item.title: Prepaid Montenegro eSIM | Crnogorski Telekom & One
item.description: Montenegro has quietly become one of Europe’s most generous tourist-data markets: 500 GB for €15 over 15 days from any of its three operators, with 5G from all of them and eSIMs you can buy online before you even land. It also has a trap that catches visitors who buy a kiosk SIM without registering it — and it is not in the EU, so European travelers who assume their home plan roams here at no cost get a painful surprise. This guide covers the three carriers with their actual tourist plans, the Western Balkans roaming that turns one eSIM into a six-country pass, and the mountains-vs-coast coverage split that decides your choice. The sticking points below are the ones that trip up first-time Montenegro eSIM users most often.

item.title: Prepaid Namibia eSIM Data | MTC, TN Mobile & Paratus
item.description: Namibia spreads roughly three million people across a country the size of France and Germany combined, so “coverage” here is really about how far past the last town your eSIM keeps working. MTC dominates and is the only operator with a genuine rural footprint — but here is the trap most travellers miss: the big international eSIM apps (Airalo, Nomad and others) selling a “Namibia eSIM” roam onto TN Mobile, not MTC, and TN Mobile’s reach outside the cities is thin. The profile you buy for the safari is therefore often not the network that covers the safari. What follows explains how to spot that gap and close it.

item.title: Prepaid New Zealand eSIM | Spark, One NZ & 2degrees
item.description: Choosing a New Zealand eSIM means picking between three networks that win different awards — this guide matches each one to the drives you have planned. On Ookla’s H1 2025 New Zealand report, One NZ was named Best Mobile Network, while Spark was the fastest 5G network and 2degrees led on consistency and fixed broadband. Where you drive decides which of them deserves your data. What does Roami’s support inbox see most for New Zealand? The same failures the coverage and registration sections below spell out.

item.title: Travel Myanmar eSIM | MPT, Ooredoo & ATOM Coverage
item.description: Which carrier a Myanmar eSIM should attach to comes with a preface most travel pages skip: the mobile market here has been reshaped since 2021, and connectivity takes more planning than anywhere else in Southeast Asia. We keep the claims conservative and cite each one. Underneath that reality check the split is straightforward — MPT owns the broadest footprint, especially beyond the cities; ATOM, the network Telenor once built, is the steadiest bet along the tourist corridors; and Mytel is large but military-linked, so many visitors pick one of the other two. Set aside a few minutes, no more — no step below has ever taken our test users longer.

item.title: Travel Nepal eSIM | Nepal Telecom, Ncell & Smart
item.description: Buying a Nepal eSIM is not a question of “which is fastest downtown” — it is “which network still has a bar on the mountain roads.” Exactly two carriers are worth the decision here: Nepal Telecom (NTC, state-owned) and Ncell (private, Axiata). A third, Smart Cell, barely registers outside the Kathmandu–Terai corridor and is not a visitor option. Where the choice is actually won or lost is beyond the cities — the Everest region, the Annapurna area, Langtang — where the towers thin out long before the villages do. The sections below cover what an eSIM in Nepal costs and where each network genuinely reaches.

item.title: Unlimited Nigeria eSIM | MTN, Airtel & Glo Coverage
item.description: Nigeria is Africa’s largest telecom market — 179.6 million active lines at the end of 2025, per the Nigerian Communications Commission — and it is also one of the hardest markets in the world to buy a Nigeria eSIM into directly. Every SIM, including every eSIM, sits behind a registration regime built around the National Identification Number (NIN), and every carrier eSIM is issued in person, with ID, at a service centre. So the real question this guide answers is not just “which carrier is fastest” but “which carrier can you actually get onto” — and for most visitors the honest answer is a travel eSIM that rides on MTN’s network without touching the KYC wall.

item.title: 5G Pakistan eSIM | Jazz, Zong & Telenor Coverage
item.description:
A Pakistan eSIM rides one of four mobile networks, and which one you land on changes what works in Karachi, what works in Hunza, and whether you can order a ride from a hotel lobby in Lahore. That is the whole decision, and this page works through it network by network, price by price.

Quick answer: the local networks win on reach and on price, and the big cities barely separate them. If eSIMs are new to you, the activation how-to comes first — the plan tables below can wait.

item.title: 5G Philippines eSIM | Globe, Smart & DITO Coverage
item.description: Which network should your Philippines eSIM call home? The three national networks are not interchangeable, and the country is an archipelago of more than seven thousand islands, so coverage is a geography problem as much as a speed problem. On Ookla’s 2H 2024 Philippines report, Smart was the fastest mobile network with a Speed Score of 72.04 and a median download of 45.83 Mbps. Globe recorded the best overall Consistency Score at 86.6%. DITO led on 5G consistency at 86.2% and on consumer sentiment at 3.65 out of 5. Which one is best depends on where you are going and how you are travelling, because the best eSIM carrier for the Philippines is a routing decision, not a brand decision. The sticking points below are the ones that trip up first-time Philippines eSIM users most often.

item.title: 5G Russia eSIM | MTS, MegaFon & Beeline Coverage
item.description: Russia is the one destination where “which carrier is best” is the third question, not the first. The first two: you cannot realistically buy a local SIM as a tourist anymore, and your eSIM will be data-blocked for roughly 24 hours after it first registers on a Russian network. Both are government policy, not operator choice, and both have changed more than once since 2025 — which is why most older guides to Russian connectivity are now actively wrong. This guide lays out the current rules with dates, the MTS vs MegaFon vs Beeline vs Tele2 reality for roaming profiles, and the day-one checklist that decides whether your Russia eSIM lands you connected or leaves you stuck.

item.title: 5G Saudi Arabia eSIM | STC, Mobily & Zain Coverage
item.description: Saudi Arabia is two connectivity markets at once: a business hub running among the fastest mobile internet anywhere, and a pilgrimage destination whose networks bend under seasonal crowds. Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index placed the kingdom 8th in the world for median mobile download in August 2026 at 224.54 Mbps, while Cable.co.uk prices a gigabyte of local data at about USD 1.49. The catch is regulatory: under the Communications, Space & Technology Commission (CST), every locally issued Saudi Arabia eSIM and SIM card is registered against your passport and your entry record. Which carrier is best therefore turns on your visa, your route, and whether you actually need a Saudi number. The Saudi Arabia questions below are the ones support answers every week — collected here in the words travelers actually use.

item.title: Oman eSIM | Omantel, Ooredoo & Vodafone Coverage
item.description: Oman is a tale of two maps, and the carrier your Oman eSIM picks decides which one you are on. Across Muscat, Salalah and Sohar every network delivers real 5G and fast downloads. Leave the covered city corridors on a coastal or intercity drive and the signal thins on a schedule that turns entirely on the operator you bought. What you are really choosing, then, is city speed against road-trip coverage — and Omantel takes the second category decisively. We have set up enough Oman eSIMs to know which steps people get wrong, and the activation guide below calls those out explicitly.

item.title: Prepaid Panama eSIM | C&W, Claro & Movistar Coverage
item.description: A Panama eSIM has a clear front-runner and a steep airport markup, and this guide covers both — plus the passport registration rule every visitor triggers. Panama is the Central American country where the carrier question has a clear answer (+Móvil owns the widest map), the airport question has a clear answer too (a 7-day unlimited tourist SIM costs about $30 at Tocumen and $10 or less in town — the steepest airport markup in the region), and the registration rule is unambiguous: passport registration for every SIM is required by law. This guide covers the four operators — including Digicel, the fourth network most recent articles quietly drop — the islands where coverage ends, and the currency quirk that makes price comparisons here unusually easy: Panama runs on US dollars.

item.title: Prepaid Portugal eSIM | MEO, NOS & Vodafone Coverage
item.description: Picking a Portugal eSIM now means choosing between four national networks rather than three, and the cheapest of them is not the slowest. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Portugal report, NOS was named the Best Mobile Network with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 79.87, MEO took the Best 5G Network award, Vodafone led on consistency and 5G availability at 80.3 percent, and the low-cost entrant Digi posted the strongest mobile gaming score at 82.23. The winner depends on the region you are touring. The rebuild cycle runs on Roami’s own Portugal activation data and tickets, with press releases as a secondary input.

item.title: Travel Norway eSIM | Telenor, Telia & Ice Coverage
item.description: Norway is the clearest coverage paradox in Europe. Its networks are world-class: Telenor took the Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network titles in the Ookla Speedtest Connectivity Report for Norway, 1H 2025 with a median 5G download of 255.4 Mbps, and Opensignal named both Telenor and ice Global Leaders for Reliability Experience in its 2025 awards. Yet data is expensive — Cable.co.uk puts 1 GB at about USD 4.07, among the priciest 15% of the 237 markets it tracks — and the geography is brutal: a single tunnel can black out your phone for twenty minutes, and the road between two covered towns can be uncovered for hours. A Norway eSIM therefore works best when you plan it like the trip itself: route by route, fjord by fjord.

item.title: Travel Peru eSIM | Claro, Movistar & Entel Coverage
item.description: A Peru eSIM handles the coast and the highlands well and the Amazon only partially, and this guide is built around knowing where the map goes dark. Peru compresses three very different countries into one itinerary: a coastal strip with fast urban networks, an Andean highland where signal follows the river valleys, and an Amazon basin where towns are islands of coverage in a green sea. A travel profile delivers the first two reliably and the third only around population centers. What separates a smooth trip from a frustrating one is not really the operator you land on — it is knowing where the coverage ends, and installing your profile before the altitude starts working on you. Picture the briefing a knowledgeable friend would hand you for Peru; that is this page, minus the jargon.

item.title: Travel Romania eSIM | Orange, Vodafone & Digi Coverage
item.description: Romania is Europe’s data-price anomaly. Locals pay about USD 0.54 per gigabyte — 50th of 237 markets, roughly a fifth of the price of data in Germany — and fixed broadband runs at 276.18 Mbps nationally, 15th in the world. Mobile speeds are more ordinary: Ookla’s August 2026 index puts the country 56th at 82.57 Mbps. For a Romania eSIM, the interesting tension is exactly there: world-class cheap data, world-class fibre, and a mobile landscape where Orange leads on speed, availability and consistency while DIGI — the discount giant that made Romanian data famously cheap — owns 5G consistency and gaming. Set aside a few minutes, no more — that is all any Romania step below has ever taken our test users.

item.title: 5G South Africa eSIM | Vodacom, MTN & Telkom Coverage
item.description: South Africa is the one major destination where the biggest eSIM factor is a law, not a network. RICA — the country’s SIM registration statute — requires every locally sold SIM to be registered in person with a passport and a South African address, which turns the airport SIM counter into an obstacle course just as your safari transfer is waiting. The networks themselves are strong: Vodacom and MTN operate genuine national 5G, and the national median of 69.57 Mbps (Ookla, August 2026) leads the region. Understanding all three layers — networks, registration law, and the geography between Cape Town and Kruger — is what a good South Africa eSIM decision actually takes.

item.title: 5G Sweden eSIM | Telia, Tele2 & Telenor Coverage
item.description: Sweden pairs two extremes that matter for your eSIM: a 5G network that is among Europe’s best, and distances in the north that can swallow an afternoon of signal. Telenor took the Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network titles in the Ookla Speedtest Connectivity Report for Sweden, 1H 2025 with a median 5G download of 234.94 Mbps; Stockholm itself measured 263.63 Mbps median mobile, the fastest Swedish city. Yet the same country runs a four-hour train between covered corridors in Norrland, and Swedish prepaid requires passport registration by law. Which carrier your Sweden eSIM should use — and how you buy one at all — is answered in the FAQ below, before anything else.

item.title: Prepaid Slovakia eSIM | Orange, Slovak Telekom & O2
item.description: Slovakia plays an unusual role in European travel connectivity: the networks are fast (Ookla ranked the country 38th globally in August 2026 at 121.19 Mbps), yet local data is priced like a premium market — USD 2.68 per gigabyte, 182nd of 237, more expensive than the global average in a region famous for cheap data. That combination shapes every Slovakia eSIM decision: the networks are worth using, the local counter is worth skipping, and the carrier choice — Telekom, Orange or the budget 4ka — matters most once you leave Bratislava for the Tatras. What does Roami’s support inbox see most for Slovakia? The same failures the coverage and registration sections below spell out.

item.title: Prepaid South Korea eSIM | SK Telecom, KT & LG U+
item.description: South Korea needs no introduction on speed — it has been a top-ten mobile country for years, and Ookla’s August 2026 index puts the national median at 250.56 Mbps, 6th in the world. What it does need is an explanation of its unusual market structure, because Korea is the rare destination where the local carriers themselves sell the best tourist products, identity rules differ for residents and visitors, and some of the apps you will want (taxi-hailing above all) quietly prefer a Korean number. Getting a South Korea eSIM right means understanding all three layers, not just the speed table — and deciding early, because South Korea’s own data market is one of the priciest in the developed world.

item.title: Prepaid Switzerland eSIM | Swisscom, Sunrise & Salt
item.description: Switzerland is the one Alpine country where your phone plan choice collides with a fact most visitors learn too late. The country sits outside the European Union and outside the EU roaming zone, so the same network that keeps you online in Zurich can bankrupt you the moment you cross into France, and a French plan that worked all the way to Basel can start billing per megabyte the second you step off the train in Geneva. This Switzerland eSIM guide compares the three Swiss carriers on verified coverage and consistency figures, lays out the prepaid eSIM routes open to foreign visitors, and explains where a single travel profile that moves between all three networks spares you the border surprise.

item.title: Spain eSIM | Movistar, Vodafone & Orange Coverage
item.description: Which network should carry your Spain eSIM? Spain is unusual in Europe because the network map reshuffled in 2024. Orange and MásMóvil merged into a single group called MásOrange, Vodafone Spain changed hands to Zegona, and Yoigo now runs as a separate brand inside MásOrange while still keeping its own radio network. The result is four physical networks visitors can actually buy onto: Movistar, MásOrange (Orange), Vodafone and Yoigo. They are not interchangeable. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Spain report, Movistar won Best Mobile Network with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 77.3 and the highest 5G availability at 78.7%. Orange posted the best gaming experience at 84.59, while Vodafone and Yoigo trailed on raw speed but remain perfectly usable in cities. Which one wins therefore follows your itinerary rather than brand loyalty: the emptier the roads, the more the choice narrows.

item.title: Taiwan eSIM | Chunghwa, Taiwan Mobile & Coverage
item.description:
A Taiwan eSIM can be genuinely unlimited and bought before you fly — one of the few destinations where both are true, because the local operators themselves sell unlimited tourist data as instant digital profiles. This guide covers who sells what, which network wins where, and how to get connected the moment you clear customs.

Quick answer: For most travellers in Taiwan, the local networks are the comfortable pick; a travel eSIM suits tighter budgets and city-only trips. Start with the eSIM compatibility quiz: the one step Taiwan travellers skip and pay for later.

item.title: Travel Singapore eSIM | Singtel, StarHub & M1 Coverage
item.description: A Singapore eSIM contest is fought indoors, not across open countryside — this guide compares the three networks on the thing that matters most in a city-state: in-building reach. Singapore is too compact for the rural coverage gaps a large country suffers, so the real contest between its three networks is how well each one reaches indoors. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Singapore report, Singtel was named Best Mobile Network and Best 5G Network, with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 87.22. StarHub and M1 sit close behind and are often cheaper for the same data. Which one is best for you depends on where you stay, how long you visit, and whether your trip spills into Malaysia or Indonesia. A Singapore eSIM is the easiest way to land already connected, and the prepaid tourist tiers from all three carriers are open to foreign passport holders. Nothing anonymous made it into this guide; the closing source list covers every Singapore figure.

item.title: Travel Thailand eSIM | AIS, TrueMove & dtac Coverage
item.description: A Thailand eSIM is only as good as the network behind it, and the gap between Thailand’s three national networks widens the further you travel from Bangkok. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Thailand report, AIS was the Best Mobile Network overall and the Best 5G Network, with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 76.05. TrueMove H posted the highest 5G Availability at 74.2%. dtac trails on raw speed but still delivers a Consistency Score of 92.5%. Which one fits therefore depends on your itinerary: the city-and-coast circuit, or the hills and the smaller Gulf islands. Marketing and reality sometimes diverge in Thailand; when they do, we say so, and the registration section carries the fine print that bites.

item.title: Tunisia eSIM | Tunisie Telecom, Ooredoo & Orange
item.description:
A Tunisia eSIM plan should not treat the country as one destination, because the coast, the capital and the southern interior behave differently — this guide splits them honestly. Most connectivity advice flattens those differences. Picture the briefing a knowledgeable friend would hand you for Tunisia; that is this page, minus the jargon.

Quick answer: Tunisie Telecom wins the coverage argument in Tunisia, and Ooredoo runs the smoothest visitor purchase — the tables below settle the details. You can also give the Tunisia network setup a spin at no cost — Roami’s free multi-network trial covers it.

item.title: 5G Turkey eSIM | Turkcell, Vodafone & Türk Telekom
item.description: Choosing which network your Turkey eSIM rides on is the one decision that shapes the whole trip, because Turkcell, Vodafone and Türk Telekom are not interchangeable. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 Türkiye report, Turkcell was named Best Mobile Network with a Speedtest Connectivity Score of 77.15, the highest Speed Score at 63.51, and the best Consistency at 93.9%. Türk Telekom followed on connectivity at 73.67 and Vodafone at 69.58. Which one is best depends entirely on where your itinerary goes, because picking a Turkey eSIM carrier is a routing decision, not a brand decision. Where do Turkey first-timers get stuck? The same few places — and each section below handles one.

item.title: 5G United States eSIM | AT&T, Verizon & T-Mobile
item.description: Choosing a United States eSIM is choosing how far you will drive: three national networks split coverage, speed and city depth across a continent-sized map, and this guide matches them to your route. The three US national networks are not interchangeable, and in a country this wide the right one depends almost entirely on your route. On Ookla’s 2H 2025 United States report, T-Mobile was the Best Mobile Network overall and the Best 5G Network, with the highest Speed Score (73.26) and the widest 5G availability (91.2%). Verizon won Best Mobile Coverage, posting a Coverage Score of 30.0% — the most geographic reach of the three. AT&T sat between them on most measures and led on the fixed broadband side. So the carrier that suits you is a question of geography: dense metros reward one network, long rural drives reward another. We can name the source behind every statement — see the list at the bottom before spending on the United States.

item.title: 5G Uruguay eSIM | Antel, Movistar & Claro Coverage
item.description: A Uruguay eSIM comes with one absolute exception worth knowing before you book: Cabo Polonio has no signal from any carrier — this guide covers that, and the passport rule at official outlets. Uruguay is South America’s quiet 5G overachiever: the state carrier Antel was an early regional adopter, blankets Montevideo and the resort coast, and holds the interior in a way no rival matches. But the country also has one of the region’s starkest coverage exceptions — Cabo Polonio, a village with no electricity grid and no signal from any carrier — and a registration rule that shapes your arrival: every SIM, foreigner included, must be tied to a passport at an official outlet. This guide covers the Antel vs Movistar vs Claro decision, the Punta del Este January congestion effect, and the Carrasco airport kiosk that closes too early for late flights. The sections on coverage and registration below are honest about the Uruguay failures our support desk fields weekly.

item.title: Prepaid Uganda eSIM | MTN, Airtel & Africell Coverage
item.description: Uganda is effectively a two-network country, and the carrier your Uganda eSIM picks turns less on raw speed than on where you are going — a Kampala business trip and a Bwindi gorilla-permit visit are two different coverage problems. MTN Uganda and Airtel Uganda together carry almost all the traffic. There is a second, very Ugandan reason the choice matters: mobile money. MTN MoMo and Airtel Money are how the country actually pays for things, which is why a local number, and not just data, can matter even to a short-stay visitor. Roami’s Uganda activation logs and support tickets feed the periodic rebuilds of this guide; marketing copy does not. For a permit week in Bwindi, a Uganda travel eSIM bought before departure is the simpler path than any counter purchase.

item.title: Prepaid Venezuela eSIM | Movistar, Digitel & Movilnet
item.description:
A Venezuela eSIM works best when your expectations are set before boarding, and this guide covers what the networks actually deliver and where power cuts still bite. The mobile networks work, but median speeds sit far below the global norm and power interruptions have historically knocked infrastructure offline.

Quick answer: a multi-network travel eSIM if you are moving around Venezuela, any single network if you are staying in one city. Speed, price and registration details below support that split; the compatibility page clears phone issues first.

item.title: Travel Ukraine eSIM | Kyivstar, Vodafone & lifecell
item.description: A Ukraine eSIM is judged the way Ukrainians judge their own networks — not by peak speed, but by how well the connection survives a bad night — and this guide explains what the networks deliver night to night and how to get set up on arrival. In Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index for August 2026, Ukraine’s median mobile download is 90.93 Mbps — 50th worldwide, at 23 ms latency — despite wartime conditions no other European market faces. Cable.co.uk prices 1 GB of Ukrainian mobile data at about USD 0.27, the 16th cheapest of 237 markets, against a USD 2.59 global average. DataReportal counted 56.4 million mobile connections at the start of 2025 — 147 percent of the population — and 31.5 million internet users. The right profile, then, is not the one with the flashiest headline number. It is the one whose network keeps running through power cuts and congestion, and the one you can install without standing in any queue. We timed newcomers through every Ukraine step below; none went past a few minutes. A Ukraine travel eSIM also sidesteps the counter paperwork entirely.

item.title: Travel Vietnam eSIM | Viettel, Vinaphone & Mobifone
item.description: A Vietnam eSIM should follow your itinerary’s shape — 1,600 km north to south — and this guide matches Viettel’s provincial dominance and Vinaphone’s 5G to the route you will run. Vietnam is a north–south country: more than 1,600 km from Sapa’s border peaks to the Mekong Delta, with your itinerary almost certainly touching both ends. That shape decides your eSIM more than any brand loyalty. On Ookla’s 1H 2025 Speedtest data, Viettel was the Best Mobile Network in the country with a median download of 165.03 Mbps and a consistency score of 97.4%, and it was the fastest provider in 59 of Vietnam’s 63 provinces. Vinaphone runs the fastest 5G network (median 5G download 594.16 Mbps), while Mobifone posted the best mobile video experience (74.46). Since all three switched on commercial 5G between October 2024 and June 2025 — with coverage reaching 91.2% of the population by December 2025 — the real question is not “is there 5G in Vietnam?” but “which carrier holds signal along the specific 1,600 km you are traveling?”

item.title: United Arab Emirates eSIM | Etisalat & du Coverage
item.description: A UAE eSIM is the rare travel purchase where the underlying network is not the question — the menu is. The UAE has been the fastest mobile market on earth for months: Ookla’s Speedtest Global Index put the country 1st in the world for median mobile download speed in August 2026, at 675.51 Mbps with 18 ms latency, and 2nd for fixed broadband at 382.40 Mbps. Against a worldwide mobile median of 109.05 Mbps, that is not a competitive market, it is a different category. The catch sits on the price line: Cable.co.uk prices 1 GB of UAE mobile data at roughly USD 4.61, 211th of 237 markets. Most visitors search for a Dubai eSIM rather than a country-wide product, but the airport counters sell the same two networks under either name.

item.title: United Kingdom eSIM | EE, Vodafone & O2 Coverage
item.description: Whether you call it a UK eSIM or a United Kingdom eSIM, picking between the four networks comes down to where you will actually use it. Four networks run the UK’s masts, and every prepaid brand you can buy — giffgaff, VOXI, SMARTY, iD Mobile, Lebara, Lycamobile, Tesco Mobile — is a reseller of one of them. Which host network you land on decides your speeds in London and whether you have a signal on a Highland road.
